_doc: TASK-416 (GUARD · chrome matrix) — the HAND-DECLARED /a route policy. One row per page.tsx under src/app/a (28 at writing, block 968,177). This file is the oracle; the tree is the suspect. It is derived ONCE by hand from each page's source and then frozen — every later change is a deliberate, reviewable PR-diff edit, never re-derived at test time (Astra's HOLD: a matrix derived from the tree would pass the very regression it exists to catch).
Row shape: { route, siteChrome, signedOut, alwaysRedirectTo?, gateDoor?, pending?, source? }.
siteChrome: "redirect" = under the site chrome (NEXT_PUBLIC_CONSOLE_CHROME=site) this route never renders — it redirects. "render" = the route renders under both chromes.

signedOut: "gate" = a signed-out visitor meets the operator gate (OperatorGate or the API's 401 courtesy), never the room. Declared per row so a future public-under-/a route is a deliberate policy edit.

gateDoor (optional): "api-401" = THIS row's signed-out door is the API's 401 courtesy, not an OperatorGate — the six client rooms whose page.tsx carries no OperatorGate (booking, letters, letters/[key], money, people, store; `grep -c OperatorGate` = 0 on each, derived at block 968,206 — TASK-418 fix round R2). A row WITHOUT this key must render the OperatorGate DOM to a signed-out visitor; a redirect-then-gate does not meet the gate (a signed-out gate cell fails on any redirect hop).

alwaysRedirectTo (optional): the route redirects UNCONDITIONALLY, both chromes, no cookie check — /a/live (T-330) and the six folded alias rooms (chat, decisions, mempool, mud, scar, spaces). RULE (Astra's D2, block 968,175): a row carrying alwaysRedirectTo OMITS signedOut — there is no signed-out gate to assert on a page that never renders; the oracle asserts the pair (alwaysRedirectTo present ⇔ signedOut absent) in BOTH directions.
pending (optional): a ruling owed by a later lane. /a/briefs renders today; the Q1 ruling (redirect like bots/status) lands in a later PAGE lane, and the flip is a policy edit riding that lane's PR.
source (optional): the page line the row was written from — evidence, not assertion. The four T-135 redirect rows quote their idiom's home line.

The full T-135 redirect idiom is: if (CONSOLE_CHROME === "site") redirect("/a"); — the oracle matches the FULL line, never the bare comparison (src/app/a/page.tsx:105 is a render branch, not a carrier; src/app/a/layout.tsx:30 is the switch itself).

TASK-418 (the two-build browser walker) reads this file as its expectations, per cell. Dynamic routes (/a/letters/[key], /a/studio/room/[room]) are policy rows by PATTERN; the walker substitutes its own fixture values — this policy never names fixture data.
